title: Level 5 / Full Skim
short_answer: Full skim only when Level 5 (or equivalent) is specified or CO’d — never a free upgrade from Level 4.
summary: Job Check's Text/Skim stage is not a free upgrade. Level 5 is a specified (or change-ordered) finish — GA-214 says so, and so does our money.
plain_words: Level 5 means a full skim over the whole surface, for gloss/semi-gloss or critical lighting. If the job was sold at Level 4, skimming the whole floor to silence a complaint is unpaid work unless the office turns it into a CO. Confirm the level before you start the skim.
when_to_use: Finish schedule / spec calls Level 5 or full skim
Office authorized a change order for skim
prerequisites: Level 4 substrate correct — joints and fasteners finished
Written confirmation of Level 5 or CO

steps.body: Confirm Level 5 (or equivalent full skim) is specified — finish schedule / spec — or that the office authorized a CO.
Level 4 substrate must be right first — joints and fasteners finished; skim is not a way to hide skipped coats.
Conditions: heat/humidity in range (Cold & Wet Conditions). Skim over cold damp board fails later.
Skim thin and even — topping/lightweight where appropriate; scrape ridges; sand to blend.
Raking-light QC before calling Text/Skim done on Job Check.
Prime handoff to paint — bare compound under paint is flashing waiting to happen.

warnings.title: Unpaid Level 5
warnings.body: Skimming a Level 4 job to silence a complaint without a CO is unpaid work.

warnings.title: Skim over bad Level 4
warnings.body: Skim is not a way to hide skipped coats.

quality_checks.prompt: Prime handoff planned — bare compound flashes

common_mistakes.title: Gift skim
common_mistakes.wrong: Full skim because paint looked bad
common_mistakes.right: Confirm Level 5 or get a CO
common_mistakes.why: Burns margin and trains bad expectations

troubleshooting.fix: Prime all repaired/skimmed areas before finish paint
